_comment: Committed benchmark baseline (#1099). The Bench workflow fails when a benchmark runs >`tolerance`x slower than its `mean` here, or breaches its `budgetMs` ceiling.  BLESS ON CI, NOT LOCALLY (#2211). Regenerate by dispatching the Bench workflow with `update_baseline: true` and committing the uploaded artifact. `pnpm bench:baseline` locally is for diagnosis only: macos-latest measures ~1.2-1.4x slower than the dev machine this file used to be blessed on (2026-09-20, comparing the two machine-independent controls, cosineSimilarity and meanPoolNormalize, across a local run and a CI run of the same commit). A locally-blessed entry therefore lands on CI already 1.2-1.4x 'slower', which eats most of a 1.3x tolerance — that, not a real regression, is why the tightened benches kept flapping.  THIS BASELINE IS DELIBERATELY PART-STALE. #2211 asked for a re-bless on the premise that the numbers were uniformly too loose. Half of that held: the three cold-rebuild entries carried 6-9x of dead headroom (blessed one day before the #1110 incremental-mirror fix landed and never re-blessed) and are tightened here, with budgetMs ceilings added now that two independent CI runs agree on them to within ~1%. The other half did not: seven save-path benches run SLOWER than their baselines, reproduced across three CI runs (2026-09-07, 09-14, 09-20) while the controls stayed flat. Blessing those would have recorded a real regression as the new normal and permanently blinded the gate to it, so their means are HELD at the pre-regression values and the gate stays red on them BY DESIGN.  The seven held entries are the three writeAndReindex, indexNote, and the three indexAllNotes. Read their ratios with one caveat: #2211 also fixed the writeAndReindex fixture, which used to seed `note-0.md` (one wiki-link suffix-index entry per note) and now seeds realistic nested multi-word paths (six), so those four ratios conflate a genuine regression with a bench that got 2-3x more honest about what a save costs in a real vault. Both are real costs a user pays; neither is a reason to bless. The PR that fixes the regression should re-bless them together and get a clean forward baseline. Owners: the perf epic's C2 (persistGraph), H1 (N3 mirror resets), H3 (buildLinkResolveCtx rebuilt per save).  FIELDS. `budgetMs`: optional absolute ceiling in ms (a scale-envelope gate) on top of the ratio check. `tolerance`: optional per-benchmark override of the top-level ratio gate. `gate: false`: track for week-over-week diffing but never fail on it. Note what is NOT here any more: the 1.3x tolerances the two queryGraph entries used to carry. Two CI runs of the same code put the tag-filter bench at 1.03ms and 1.89ms — an 1.8x spread between runs — so a 1.3x gate on it could only ever flap. They sit at the file default now.  THE SIX gate:false ENTRIES (persistGraph + queryGraph, runAllChecks) are new in #2211 and exist to measure the known-slow code the perf epic's C1 and C2 describe. They reproduce both findings immediately: persist-then-query costs 97/315/965ms at 500/2000/5000 notes, against 3.2/7.4/15.8ms for the ordinary save-then-query next to it — persisting makes the same query roughly 60x more expensive at 5k. runAllChecks, which runs debounced off every graph write, costs 307/1151/2619ms. They are tracked rather than gated on purpose: the Bench job had already been failing unread for a fortnight, and adding six more permanently-red entries buys visibility nobody was reading. Turn gating on in the PR that fixes each.
